pull.title: guix: build glibc with `--enable-kernel=3.17.0`
pull.body: Our minimum required kernel version is documented as `3.17.0`. Pass `--enable-kernel=3.17.0` when building glibc, so that version is reflected in the binary, and the version checked in the symbol-check script, aligns with the expected minimum.

Concept ACK. I was about suggesting the same in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/25573.

> Our minimum required kernel version is documented as `3.17.0`. Pass `--enable-kernel=3.17.0` when building glibc, so that version is reflected in the binary, and the version checked in the symbol-check script, aligns with the expected minimum.

[Also](https://sourceware.org/glibc/manual/latest/html_node/Configuring-and-compiling.html):
>  The higher the version number is, ... the faster the code gets.

ACK 5548818115c02d1e452a3240593b6e929c387d1d, tested on Ubuntu 24.04:
```console
$ file bin/bitcoind
bin/bitcoind: ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64, version 1 (GNU/Linux), dynamically linked, interpreter /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1, for GNU/Linux 3.17.0, stripped
```

> [Also](https://sourceware.org/glibc/manual/latest/html_node/Configuring-and-compiling.html):
> 
> > The higher the version number is, ... the faster the code gets.

I don't know how much difference it will actually make, but even the very oldest OSes are generally newer than 3.17: https://repology.org/project/linux/versions

bumping to 4.18 woudl bring us in line with CentOS 8, and 5.10 is the last maintained version currently...

As we have it working on 3.17 though also feels unnecessary to bump unless there is an actual (measured) performance benefit...

You can take a look through https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob;f=sysdeps/unix/sysv/linux/kernel-features.h;h=85f6e888dba58fe7e4b27fc594d80e02092187f6;hb=HEAD, to get an idea of what is actually effected by changing the supplied kernel version.
